name: Katalin Nagy
institution: Hungarian Academy of Sciences / Semmelweis University
description: Katalin Nagy leads Hungary's foremost research program in oral microbiome ecology, with a particular focus on how dysbiotic shifts in subgingival biofilm communities drive systemic inflammatory disease including cardiovascular disease, rheumatoid arthritis, and adverse pregnancy outcomes. Her longitudinal cohort studies in Budapest established quantitative thresholds of Porphyromonas gingivalis and Treponema denticola abundance that predict incident atherosclerosis, providing the first Eastern European population data integrated into European oral health guidelines. Nagy pioneered anaerobic culturing combined with next-generation sequencing protocols adapted for clinical microbiology labs with limited infrastructure, a methodology now adopted at twelve university hospitals across Central and Eastern Europe. She received the Albert-Wander Prize from the European Society for Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism and has been a visiting researcher at King's College London's Dental Institute. Her collaborative work with Richter Gedeon is developing a bacteriocin-based topical therapy targeting periodontal pathogens.
